findings.detail: The `Also recorded here: approved behaviour, not a defect` block lives inside the Fix recommendation cell of TD-055, whose status is `open` and whose content is four unrelated Low code findings. This document's own convention (line 3: "closed items move to the bottom") moves a closed entry into the `## Closed` table, which has only four columns — ID, Description, Closed, Fixed by (line 54-55). The Fix recommendation cell is not carried across that move. So the moment the four Lows are fixed and TD-055 closes, the standing instruction `Do not "fix" it without a new product decision` silently disappears from the register — which is precisely the audience (a future reader re-deriving why the flag stays TRUE) the note was written for. The note is accurate and its cross-reference resolves; only its storage location is fragile. This stays low rather than medium because the canonical decision record already exists independently at docs/modules/open-decisions.md:287 (D12 rule 7), so nothing is lost outright — what is lost is the pointer from the register to it.
findings.summary: Approved-behaviour record is stored in a row that will be archived when TD-055 closes
